finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::timezone fix misses date/time array oids — timestamp[]/date[] are still parsed into js dates shifted by the node runtime timezone
evidence: datasource.service.ts:20-24 lists only the scalar OIDs DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ, and datasourceTypeParser (lines 33-36) delegates all other OIDs to pg-types' default parser; pg-types registers the array OIDs 1115/1182/1185 to an array-of-date parser that uses the same timezone-sensitive parseDate, so timestamp[]/date[] still yield JS Dates and toCell (readonly.ts:31-35) JSON.stringifies them into shifted ISO strings. The added `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` does not help, since the local-time interpretation of naive timestamps happens in the Node parser, not in Postgres output. The claim's extension to composite/row and range types is wrong — pg-types leaves those as raw text — but that does not undermine the array-OID gap. Confidence is medium because no checkout was mounted, so the pg-types array parser registration is from library knowledge rather than source I read; impact is limited to array-typed date/time columns plus an inconsistency with the scalar rendering.
